adoption.rationale: README enum semantics and the exact source call path establish that schema enum values are displayed by EnumEditor; the three ordered replacements run in the string branch before the result is assigned to display_area.innerHTML. The contract is limited to string leaves from application schema configuration and their HTML text rendering.

contract.declared_domain: Exact frozen 20-r2 pin b31ddabecf4ed3209d37a2f5b29956120cd8f9ce and src/editors/enum.js SHA-256 315aae54dbaf602bb25c08c064187805a3ac279a61aae8cd6d4d49eec0c44b14. The Z3 proof domain is one Unicode codepoint through the exact per-codepoint image of the ordered three-replacement string branch, with no length bound on that token. The source uses global single-character replacements in ampersand/less-than/greater-than order; an exact Node gate checks the real whole-string method over every Unicode scalar value, short exhaustive strings, targeted payloads, and seeded strings. This does not claim a formal whole-string theorem for other EnumEditor values, object keys, attributes, URLs, or script/style contexts.
contract.guarantee: For each string leaf in an application schema's enum value, the pinned EnumEditor.getHTML string branch applies the ordered ampersand, less-than, and greater-than replacements before the result reaches display_area.innerHTML. Each such codepoint is emitted as its corresponding HTML text entity, so it is displayed as text rather than parsed as element markup. This claim is limited to string leaves; object keys and non-string values are outside the contract.
contract.input_source: String leaves from the application-provided schema.enum values, passed through EnumEditor.build and getHTML into the selected-value display_area.innerHTML sink.

domain: One Unicode codepoint passed through the pinned, ordered EnumEditor string replacements contains no raw less-than or greater-than delimiter
